external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed node installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway
external_entities.notes: Nodes are outside our physical control and may be physically accessible to a technician.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views telemetry dashboards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts readings from sensor nodes and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that picks up readings from Pub/Sub and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

processes.name: dashboard
processes.description: A dashboard used by fleet operators to view telemetry over BigQuery.
processes.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used by the device gateway to check a device key and identify its customer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A messaging service onto which the device gateway forwards accepted readings and from which the telemetry normalizer picks them up.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing site addresses and occupancy patterns, which are customer data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll for new firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. It is unknown whether nodes check an image signature before installing it.

data_flows.name: readings
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes publish readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway
data_flows.authentication: pre-shared key (per fleet, not per device)

data_flows.name: device lookup
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up a device in the registry to check the key and determine the customer to which the node belongs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: accepted readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings to Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: normalized readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery
data_flows.data_description: sensor readings, including site addresses and occupancy patterns

data_flows.name: firmware poll
data_flows.description: Sensor nodes poll the firmware bucket for a new image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: serial service
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: Authentication on the console is unknown: "I don't know what authentication that console has, if any."

data_flows.name: dashboard view
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

data_flows.name: dashboard query
data_flows.description: The dashboard accesses telemetry in BigQuery for fleet operators.

trust_boundaries.description: A customer-controlled site where sensor nodes are installed and serviced.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public network from which sensor nodes connect to the device gateway.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: expose to the internet because the nodes dial in from anywhere

trust_boundaries.name: GKE
trust_boundaries.description: The GKE environment in which the device gateway runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: an MQTT broker we run on GKE

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the telemetry normalizer and associated telemetry services.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network
trust_boundaries.notes: The placement of the managed data stores in this zone is inferred from their role in the analytics pipeline.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators access dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is in the analytics network because it is a managed backend store used by the telemetry pipeline; the text does not state its network location.
assumptions.basis: The description identifies the analytics network for the telemetry normalizer but does not separately place the Firestore device registry.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub is in the analytics network because it connects the device gateway to the telemetry normalizer; the text does not state its network location.
assumptions.basis: Pub/Sub is the messaging store used by the analytics pipeline, while the only explicitly named backend network is the analytics network.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is in the analytics network because it stores the output of the telemetry normalizer; the text does not state its network location.
assumptions.basis: The lake is the BigQuery destination of the normalizer in the analytics network.

assumptions.assumption: The firmware bucket is in the analytics network because it is a managed platform store associated with the telemetry system; the text does not state its network location.
assumptions.basis: The description names Cloud Storage but gives no separate network zone for it.
It contains site addresses and occupancy patterns and is explicitly described as customer data.
It contains device keys and customer associations.
